description: WHERE A PICTURE GOES. `destinations` is the registry: one entry = one place a generated picture ends up (a platform surface), with the exact ratio and pixels it needs, WHY the picture is there and HOW it gets there. A set says `for: [destination ids]`, the director takes the ratio to generate from here (`generate_as`), scripts/export_ads.py cuts the delivery files from the finished frames, scripts/run_board.py shows which destinations a frame serves. Code: reels_pipeline/destinations.py. `platforms` below it are the checked facts of the official pages (Meta help pages and Meta MCP, Pinterest Business help, Google Ads and Merchant Center help, checked 2026-11-06) the destinations are made from. The upload itself (step B) is NOT built: `how` only names the tool that will do it.

fields.tag: the platform: meta | pinterest | google | etsy | feed. The id of a destination starts with it, and so does the name of a frame made for it (<set>_<pair><n>_<colour>_<tag>_<ratio>), so it is clear later where a file goes
fields.ratio: the exact delivery ratio 'W:H' (null = the destination takes any ratio, it cannot decide what to generate)
fields.tolerance: how far the real ratio may be from `ratio` (0.03 = 3%; Meta 3%, Google 1%)
fields.generate_as: the ratio to ask the model for (an exact KIE aspect_ratio); differs from `ratio` only when the delivery is a centre crop of it (1.91:1 is cut from 16:9)
fields.crop_max: the most a centre crop may remove from the cut side (0 = never crop)
fields.min_px: [width, height] below which the platform refuses or blurs the picture (null = not stated)
fields.needs: what every delivery file must have: 'ai_label' = IPTC DigitalSourceType trainedAlgorithmicMedia (Google Merchant: every AI-made image)
fields.clip_source: true = the frame is also the first frame of a Kling clip for a REEL: a reel needs DIFFERENT designs, so a carousel pair (one design in other colours) for it is refused unless the pair says purpose: stories_carousel
fields.status: live = used today; planned = we can generate it but nothing uses it yet; open = an owner decision is missing
fields.video: the delivery spec of a VIDEO for this destination (read by reels_pipeline/video_check.py, `scripts/check_reel.py`): `meta` = what the platform's own help says, `advice` = what practitioners recommend (the platform publishes no number); a check against `advice` is a warning, against `meta` an error

meta_stories_reels.platform: Meta (Instagram / Facebook Reels and Stories); the same frame is the first frame of a Kling clip for Reels, YouTube Shorts and Pinterest video
meta_stories_reels.why: full-screen vertical placements and the first frame of every reel clip; keep the top and bottom 14% (250 px) free of the main subject and of any text
meta_stories_reels.goes_to: Meta ad account 1591946192121461, Instagram @moonbloomwalls, YouTube, Pinterest ad account 549770501688
meta_stories_reels.how: Meta MCP ads_creative_upload_media / ads_creative_upload_local_image; Kling 2.6 takes the frame as its image (ComfyUI video board)

audio.note: Meta recommends music or sound for Reels ads

advice.fps: keep the native constant rate (24 from Grok / Kling); do not resample 24 to 30 (duplicated frames judder)
rules: export the final reel in ONE pass: every extra export or a 'compress for sharing' switch is another re-encode
never upload a file saved from another app or sent through a messenger
upload over Wi-Fi with high-quality uploads switched on in the Instagram app
do not export 4K: the platform downsizes it anyway; 1080x1920 is the target

meta_feed_ad.platform: Meta (Facebook feed, Instagram feed, carousel of catalog ads)
meta_feed_ad.why: the ad image of the feed: Facebook feed recommends 4:5, Instagram feed takes it, an Advantage+ catalog carousel takes 4:5 or 1:1 and fits every card to the FIRST one

meta_square.platform: Meta (Shops, catalog carousel in 1:1), Pinterest collections secondary images
meta_square.why: Meta Shops show product images 1:1 and a carousel that starts with a square keeps every card square; Pinterest collections prefer 1:1 secondary images

pinterest_pin.platform: Pinterest (organic pin in the feed, promoted pin = the same pin as an ad, catalog image_link)
pinterest_pin.why: ONE file for three uses: the standard Pin is 2:3 and is published organically in the feed OR promoted as an ad (Pinterest: a standard image ad can be used in paid campaigns or to generate organic impressions; an ad is an existing pin put into promotion), and a catalog image_link must be at least 1000x1500; taller than 1:2.1 is cut off in the feed
pinterest_pin.goes_to: Pinterest profile (organic), Pinterest ad account 549770501688 (promotion), catalog 'MoonBloom Products DE'
pinterest_pin.how: organic: Etsy/pinterest/bulk (CSV) or by hand; ad: the Pinterest MCP create_pinterest_ad on the published pin; catalog: the feed

google_search_landscape.platform: Google Ads (images of the Search campaign, PMax / Demand Gen horizontal)
google_search_landscape.why: image extension of the Search campaign 24386071357; the Google Ads MCP tool cuts to 1.91:1 itself, we deliver the exact ratio so nothing important is cut
google_search_landscape.goes_to: Google Ads Search campaign 24386071357 (MoonBloom Search DE+AT - Site)
google_search_landscape.how: Google Ads MCP create_image_asset (dry_run first; the file must be on moonbloomwalls.com, the tool downloads it from the site)

google_search_square.platform: Google Ads (images of the Search campaign, PMax / Demand Gen square)
google_search_square.why: the square image of the Search campaign

etsy_gallery.platform: Etsy listing gallery (the site takes its photos from the listing, in Etsy order)
etsy_gallery.why: Etsy recommends 4:3 for the first thumbnail; the site and the feed take the listing photos in this order, so the FIRST Etsy photo becomes the feed's main image
etsy_gallery.goes_to: Etsy shop 64001040 listing, then site card photos (markup_photos)
etsy_gallery.how: by hand in Etsy, then Etsy/site/scripts/sync_listing_media.py

feed_main.platform: google_shopping_feed.xml image_link (Merchant Center, Meta catalog, Pinterest catalog read ONE file)
feed_main.why: the main picture of every item in three catalogs at once; today it is the first photo of the Etsy listing, which is 4:3 for some items; Meta fits all carousel cards to its ratio (min 500x500), Pinterest wants it at least 1000x1500 (a horizontal one only gets a warning). Google asks for the product itself in image_link and the shop has a Misrepresentation issue since 2026-11-04
feed_main.goes_to: Merchant Center 5882676064, Meta catalog 1119303930493909, Pinterest catalog
feed_main.how: Etsy/site: card JSON -> build -> feed (a pull request there, deploy only on the owner's yes)

feed_additional.why: interiors and details; Meta uses a 9:16 one for Stories when 'Adapt to placement' is on; Pinterest makes a pin of each one (a horizontal one only gets a warning)
feed_additional.how: Etsy/site: the listing photos after the first

feeds: Meta catalog 'MoonBloom Walls' (id 1119303930493909, its only data source, replaced every day 06:00 Berlin)
feed.lives_in: the website project nocode/Etsy/site (feed/product_feed.py), not this repository
feed.note: Meta fits every card of a carousel/collection to the ratio of the FIRST image, so the first image of an item decides how the whole ad looks. Some items have a 4:3 first image.

4:5.only: Advantage+ catalog ads in carousel format with catalog product images

meta_catalog_carousel.rule: all images of an ad in ONE ratio; other ratios are fitted (zoom crop, or white space) to the first image; ratio tolerance 3%
crop_settings: Commerce Manager > catalog settings: Fill frame (default) | Show entire image (white space) | Crop and resize
Ads Manager > ad > Image touch-ups: overrides the catalog setting
meta_catalog_carousel.file: JPEG or PNG, catalog image up to 8 MB (ad image up to 30 MB); WebP is not listed in the docs

meta_stories_reels.safe_zone: keep about 14% (250 px) at the top and the bottom free of text and logos
meta_stories_reels.catalog_ads: a 9:16 catalog image is shown full screen when 'Adapt to placement' is on and the product has a 9:16 image; one older help page says catalog ads in Stories use 1.91:1: check the preview in Ads Manager

meta_single_image.instagram_feed: all of 1.91:1 to 4:5 supported; 1:1 and 4:5 recommended for images

standard_pin.note: taller than 1:2.1 (2:4.2) is cut off in the feed

pinterest.collections: hero 1:1 or 2:3; all secondary images ONE ratio (1:1 recommended, a non-square one is centre-cropped)
pinterest.file: PNG or JPEG, up to 20 MB (desktop) / 32 MB (app)

google_shopping_from_feed.observed: an ad image from the owner's account (tpc.googlesyndication.com/pimgad/16540975458122580645) is a 1005x1005 square JPEG; whether Google crops or pads a non-square feed image was not checked
google_shopping_from_feed.owner_campaigns: Shopping from the Merchant Center feed; the other campaigns are Search
google_shopping_from_feed.image_rules: image_link shows the product itself, no promotional text, watermark or border; staging and in-use pictures are allowed in additional_image_link (https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/7052112)

google_ai_label.rule: every image made with generative AI must carry the IPTC DigitalSourceType trainedAlgorithmicMedia in its metadata and the tag must not be removed

google_search_assets.tool: Google Ads MCP create_image_asset (nocode/Etsy/google-ads/tools/image_tools.py): downloads from moonbloomwalls.com, centre-cuts to 1.91:1 or 1:1 (1% tolerance), min 600x314 / 300x300, width up to 1200

google_pmax_demand_gen.rule: content in the centre 80% of the image; up to 5 MB; JPG or PNG
